item.description:
### Added
- Right-click the diff mask button, in the preview or the grid, to set how opaque the mask is over the golden, and tap the colour dot beside the slider to paint changed pixels red, green or blue. Both are also in Settings and are remembered. Changing them doesn't diff the images again. - Search the pull requests in the review dialog: type a number, words from the title, an author or a branch. The list filters as you type, and GitHub and GitLab are searched too, so it finds pull requests the list hasn't loaded, and on GitHub its search syntax works too, such as `author:alice is:merged`. Type a number and press Enter to open that pull request straight away. Azure DevOps can only find a pull request by its number, so there the field takes just that. - The review dialog shows the pull requests it loaded last time at once and refreshes them in the background. A refresh button next to the filter reloads them.
### Changed
- The review dialog is taller and wider, and keeps its size while the pull requests load, so nothing jumps. Quick and Custom are at the top, and the pull request list fills the rest, showing when each was last updated. Its rows no longer show a tooltip that covered the titles. - When a golden's variant chips don't fit in the preview toolbar, they move under it, as wide as the preview, and wrap onto more lines so you can see all of them at once. If they'd take more than a third of the preview's height, they scroll up and down there. A few short variants stay in the toolbar as before.
### Fixed
- Starting a review while the grid is open now shows the loader over the grid, so switching from one review to another no longer looks frozen while the pull request is fetched. Messages such as a review that couldn't start show over the grid too. - Reviewing a pull request that merged a newer base branch than your clone has fetched no longer shows the base branch's changes as the pull request's. The review now compares against the base commit your git host uses, fetching it when your clone doesn't have it, as the host's own "Files changed" does. - Pressing G, or the Grid button, while no golden is selected now opens the grid on every golden, as when a review has just started, instead of doing nothing.

### Fixed
- Opening another golden now scrolls its variant chips so the selected one is in the middle, also when it has the same name as the variant you had open and when the chips first appear.

### Fixed
- Reviewing a pull request that adds or changes a variant now shows all of that golden's variants, in the preview's chips and in the grid, so you can compare a new variant with the ones already there. The ones the review didn't change are dimmed, opening a golden still lands on a variant that changed, and counts still count only changed images.

### Fixed
- Typing a variant pattern in Settings no longer breaks the dialog partway through: any pattern that compiles works, with or without a `(?<variant>…)` group, and a match that would leave a golden without a name keeps the file as it is.

### Fixed
- When security software such as Santa blocks the odiff that comes with the app, it uses odiff from Homebrew instead, and asks to start the blocked one only once per launch instead of on every diff. - Comparing images of different sizes no longer shows changes above 100%, such as "890880%": the share is now of the bigger image. - When an update can't install, for example because security software blocks Sparkle's installer, the popover offers the Homebrew command that updates instead, with a button to copy it. - Each tick of the grid's thumbnail size slider gives a different size; at some window widths, two neighbouring ticks gave the same.

### Improved
- A slider in the grid's toolbar, or + and − on the keyboard, sets how big the thumbnails are, from small enough to see many goldens at once to large enough to check details, and the grid remembers it. - The sidebar takes less indent: a folder holding only another folder shows as one row, like `pages/home`, and a folder holding only one golden shows as that golden, with a folder of pictures for its icon: `other/login`, or just `files` when the golden is named like its folder. - While you type a variant pattern in Settings, it shows how many goldens it gives variants and how many images they hold, so you can tell it matches before saving. - Counts read the same everywhere, goldens and the images they hold: "12 goldens (31 images)" in the sidebar, the grid and Settings, and "3 images changed" on the timeline. The grid's toolbar shows just that, without which commits it compares. - The breadcrumbs above the preview show what the grid shows while it's open, and each one opens the grid there: the project the Grid overview, a folder its goldens, a golden its variants.

### Improved
- Dates and times follow your Mac's region and the date format chosen in System Settings, such as day-first dates and a 24-hour clock, instead of always the US style: on the timeline, in commit details, the branch picker, recent projects and Settings. - Swift snapshots (`__Snapshots__`) and Android Compose screenshot tests (`screenshotTest…`) show up without changing any settings, next to Flutter goldens and Paparazzi snapshots under `test/`. Projects still on the old Flutter-only default switch to the new one. **Goldens globs** in Project settings now takes several patterns, one per line.
### Fixed
- While Settings or another dialog is open, keyboard shortcuts and the menu bar no longer act on the app behind it: for example, G no longer opens the grid after you've clicked out of a field in Settings. - The grid's toolbar no longer cuts its title and what it shows ("latest", "vs …") short while there's room for them. - The grid's timeline follows renamed and moved goldens, as a golden's own timeline does: it shows the commits from before the rename, and picking one shows the golden as it was then. Before, its history stopped at the rename. A tile whose golden was only renamed between A and B says **renamed** instead of `=`, and hovering over its change shows the golden's name at A and at B. - The welcome screen says Golden Browser is for Flutter golden, Swift snapshot and Android screenshot tests, not only Flutter, and the Open dialog no longer asks for a Flutter project.
No changes in the app itself: this version only changes how it's built.

### Changed
- If you agreed to help improve Golden Browser, the usage statistics now include which features you use and whether you reach them with the keyboard, a menu or a click: for example that you used the slider or opened the grid. Never what you were looking at: no file names, branches or pull requests. - The crosshair is now one button in the toolbar and one item in the View menu that switch it on and off, like Find Diff Pixels, instead of separate On and Off. - The View menu marks what's on with a tick instead of a bullet.
### Fixed
- Starting a review while the pull request list was still loading no longer causes an error in the background. - Changing the pull request filter while the list was loading no longer mixes in pull requests from the previous filter.

### New
- **Help improve Golden Browser, if you want to** — after you sign in, the app asks once whether it may send crash reports and anonymous usage statistics, and switch on new features for you as they're rolled out gradually. You can change your answer in Settings, and nothing is sent without a yes. File paths are removed first, and nothing from your repositories or images is sent.
### Fixed
- Installing odiff while the app is open takes effect when you come back to it: the warning goes away and the diffs that failed fill in, without a restart. - The grid now says when odiff is missing, and with **Only differing pixels** a tile that couldn't be diffed says so instead of looking unchanged. - If the odiff that comes with the app can't run, the warning says to reinstall Golden Browser instead of suggesting Homebrew.

### Improved
- While you sign in, the app shows a short code. Check that your browser shows the same code before you click **Connect this device**, so you only ever connect your own sign-in.

**Requires macOS 13 Ventura or later.** Macs on macOS 12 stay on 0.4.0.
### New
- **odiff comes with the app** — pixel diffs and the timeline's change indicators work out of the box, without installing odiff from Homebrew. - **About and Acknowledgements** — the Golden Browser menu now has **About** (the version, and links to the website, terms and privacy policy) and **Acknowledgements** (the open-source software inside the app and its licences), plus **Settings…**, **Hide** and **Quit**. The links to the terms and privacy policy are also under Settings → Account. - **⌘,** opens Settings; holding **⌘** shows it on the settings button.
### Improved
- Signing out frees this Mac's place in your account's machine limit, so you can sign in on another Mac straight away, without signing this one out on the website. - Your sign-in is kept in the macOS Keychain. - When the app can't confirm your licence, the lock screen says why: the licence server can't be reached, the app is too old for your licence, your Mac's clock is off, or the licence couldn't be verified. A failed sign-in is explained in plain words.
### Fixed
- After signing in, the menu bar had no **Quit**, **Hide** or **About**, and **⌘Q** did nothing. - The licence is checked again when it expires, even if the app stays open in front the whole time.

### New
- **Grid view** — see many goldens side by side in place of the preview: a golden's variants, every golden in a folder, or all of them with **Grid overview** at the top of the sidebar, which also shows as you move onto it, like a golden does. Open the grid with **G**, the **Grid** button at the end of the preview toolbar, a folder's grid button, or a right-click menu. While it's open the grid follows the sidebar — click or W/S onto a folder or a golden and the grid shows it — until **G**, **Esc** or **Close grid**. Click a tile to open that image in the preview. - The grid has its own timeline: every commit that changed its goldens, with how many changed between the chips. Pick A and B there to see each tile at A, its change against B beside its name, and the diff overlay and **Find diff pixels** on every tile. - **Grid in review mode** — the grid shows a review's changed images, compared between the review's two sides. A deleted golden shows faded at its old version. - **LFS goldens in the grid** — a tile that isn't downloaded has a **Load** button, and a bar above the grid offers **Load all** and **Always load in this project**. - **Hold ⌥, ⌘ or ⌃ to see shortcuts** — after half a second, every button with a shortcut shows its keys underneath, and the sidebar, timeline, preview and grid list the keys that act on them, until you let go. - **Sort the grid** from the first buttons in its toolbar, or cycle with **R**: as in the sidebar, changed first, or biggest change first, where added and deleted images lead and a golden's variants can part. - The single preview now has the diff overlay (mask or only the differing pixels), **Find diff pixels** and the crosshair, like side-by-side.
### Improved
- **Q** / **E** keep the selected commit in the middle of the timeline, together with B while you compare against it. - **Enter** now also expands and collapses the focused folder, like **Space**, and both open Grid overview when it's focused. - The crosshair always snaps to image pixels, so there's one crosshair button instead of smooth and pixel-snap ones, and **X** turns it on and off. - The branch picker works from the keyboard: **↑** / **↓** move through branches and tags, or the search's matches, and **Enter** picks one. - The branch button gives its whole width to the branch name, with HEAD as a small badge on its corner; in the picker, HEAD sits at the end of its row, where a remote's name does.
### Fixed
- Switching branches could break the sidebar with errors until the app was restarted. - Switching back to the app reloaded what it showed every time, visibly; it now refreshes only when the repo changed meanwhile. - With thousands of goldens, Grid overview's timeline and sorting by biggest change no longer freeze the app.

### New
- **Updates from inside the app** — when a new version is out, a button appears next to **Back to projects**, or next to Settings on the welcome and sign-in screens. It shows what's new, downloads the update in the background, and installs it when you restart Golden Browser, or the next time you quit. This version still needs `brew upgrade --cask golden-browser`; later ones arrive in the app.
